findings.title: Scope and Limitations' AttributeError-on-typo guarantee is false, independently reproduced, and was never checked by facts.json
findings.detail: The live README (and therefore both byte-identical candidates) states: 'Assigning to a property a shape or a formatting object does not have raises AttributeError rather than being silently accepted and discarded, so a misspelt property name fails where it is written; names beginning with an underscore are unaffected.' Independently reproduced against the installed PyPI package (aspose-slides-foss 26.8.0, the same release facts.json verified its other 5 claims against) to be false: assigning an arbitrary nonexistent attribute to a Shape/AutoShape instance, a FillFormat instance, and a LineFormat instance each succeeds silently with no exception, and the value reads back correctly afterward. Reproduced in two separate fresh Python processes with different attribute names across all three object types to rule out a fluke. Source inspection (no __setattr__ override, no __slots__, anywhere in the 572-file installed package tree) confirms the mechanism: there is no code path in the shipped package that could raise AttributeError on an unknown attribute name. facts.json's own summary states only '5 precise, independently checkable claims verified this pass' -- this claim was never one of the 5, so it reached both candidates completely unverified, under a disposition scheme (SUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED/UNVERIFIED) that mission authority requires for every claim. Per mission-authority's own rule, 'not verified' must never be silently presented as true; here a never-verified claim is not just presented as true but is demonstrably false. This is a specific, deterministic, twice-reproduced refutation, not a stylistic or coverage objection.

Because the final document is byte-identical to the live README, the diff-scoping gap had negligible practical impact in this specific case. The content_units.json gap is more consequential: there is no artifact in this directory enumerating which README sections or individual claims were considered and dispositioned (vs. simply left alone by default), and the absence of such a ledger is plausibly why F1 -- a false, falsifiable claim sitting in the most safety-critical section of the README -- was never flagged by the pipeline that produced this candidate.

verdict_rationale: F1 (the false AttributeError-on-typo guarantee in Scope and Limitations) was fixed by the supervisor session 2026-10-21, after independently re-reproducing the review's own finding once more from a fresh pip install (aspose-slides-foss 26.8.0 in a new venv) before touching anything: assigning an arbitrary unknown attribute to a Shape/AutoShape, a FillFormat, and a LineFormat instance each succeeded silently with no exception and read back correctly, in two separate fresh processes, with zero `__setattr__`/`__slots__` matches anywhere in the installed package tree -- this independently reconfirms F1's claim rather than merely trusting its prose. lane_l_candidate.md's Scope and Limitations bullet was corrected to state the true behavior: silent assignment, no validation or error of any kind, and a misspelt property name fails silently (creates a harmless unused attribute) rather than being caught. facts.json was updated to add this newly-confirmed fact (F-ATTRIBUTEERROR-ON-TYPO-FALSE, CONTRADICTED) -- it was never checked by the original composer's 5-fact pass. A `diff` against a freshly re-fetched live README (current main HEAD, matching source_revision, no drift) confirms lane_l_candidate.diff now accurately reflects exactly this one correction and nothing else. Verdict updated from REJECT to ACCEPT after the fix; this is not a retroactive downgrade of the finding -- F1 stands as correctly identified and is marked 'fixed', not erased, per this project's AGENTS.md re-reporting discipline. F2 (missing lane_l_candidate.diff / content_units.json) is partially addressed: lane_l_candidate.diff now exists for this repository; content_units.json remains absent and is still recommended, non-blocking. Enterprise Edition naming (C6) was already fully compliant and required no change.
